project_type: Deterministic anti-overfitting XAUUSD (Gold) trading-strategy validation lab. Python detection + rule-engine + variant simulation on real repo OHLC, feeding an existing deterministic validation pipeline. MT5 (.mq5) EAs are the eventual real-tick executor but are out of scope for these Python blocks.
language: Python (detection/rule-engine/validation). MQL5 exists in repo but not touched by this task.
build_system: None. Plain Python scripts run directly (python3 <script>). No package manager step.
test_framework: Self-check convention: each module has a built-in `--selfcheck` (or `selfcheck()`) that runs synthetic deterministic assertions with plain `assert` and prints 'selfcheck: PASS'. pytest is NOT installed. Do NOT introduce pytest; follow the existing `v1_lab/qm_detect.py --selfcheck` pattern exactly.
build_command: python3 -c "import py_compile,glob; [py_compile.compile(f,doraise=True) for f in glob.glob('v1_lab/*.py')]"  (byte-compile check; there is no real build)
test_command: Run each module's self-check, e.g. `python3 v1_lab/qm_detect.py --selfcheck`, then a real-data run e.g. `python3 v1_lab/qm_detect.py v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv`. New modules must add their own `--selfcheck` and be runnable on v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv or XAUUSD_M5_clean.csv.
verification_instructions: For each block: (1) run the module's --selfcheck and confirm it prints PASS with synthetic assertions covering the LOCKED behavior and the no-lookahead property; (2) run it on real repo data (v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv, 22849 bars, and/or M5) and record detection counts; (3) confirm determinism by running twice and diffing output (md5 identical). The final variant-runner block additionally feeds generated per-variant trade CSVs (pipeline format 'time,profit') into `python3 v1_lab/pipeline.py --is IS.csv --oos OOS.csv` and records the verdict per variant. Grep is NOT verification.
snapshot_or_generated_files: Detectors emit CSV artifacts (e.g. v1_lab/mss_events.csv already exists from block 1). Regenerate with the module's CLI, e.g. `python3 v1_lab/qm_detect.py v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv --out v1_lab/mss_events.csv`. These are deterministic (same input+params => identical bytes).
setup_instructions: No setup/install needed. Python 3.9 stdlib only. Work directly in /projects/sandbox/ckrepo on branch kiro/validation-toolkit. Commit locally after each block; do NOT push or open PRs.
environment_constraints: CRITICAL: Python is 3.9.25 with STDLIB ONLY. pandas, numpy, and pytest are NOT installed (orchestrator briefing said 3.11+pandas but the actual sandbox differs). ALL new code must be pure standard library, matching the existing v1_lab/qm_detect.py (csv, datetime, statistics, random, hashlib, argparse). `zoneinfo` IS available and the 'America/New_York' tz is present in the OS tzdata (verified) - usable for cross-checking DST math, but the DST rule must ALSO be implemented as explicit provable math (2nd Sunday March -> 1st Sunday November = EDT UTC-4, else EST UTC-5) and self-checked against zoneinfo. OPEN_INTERNET is available but no external data is needed for these blocks except the SMT data dependency (XAGUSD/DXY series) which are NOT in the repo.
contribution_requirements: GOVERNING RULE (inviolable, from SPEC/DESIGN_v1.0.md and SPEC/AGENT_SYSTEM_v1.md): 'AI discovers and explains; deterministic code measures and judges; locked/unseen data is final evidence; no single metric equals PASS; overfitting is forbidden.' Concrete: NEVER hard-code or pre-select a best threshold/parameter. Every rule the setup creator has NOT explicitly confirmed MUST be a tunable PARAMETER (sensible default) or an explicit VARIANT switch, to be A/B-tested on out-of-sample data later. Pre-choosing a good-looking value = overfitting = FORBIDDEN. All code must be deterministic (same input+params => identical output) and causal (no lookahead / no future information at any decision timestamp). Do NOT write submission/verdict entries to SPEC/dof_ledger.jsonl (orchestrator owns those, currently seq26); you MAY append technical build entries via SPEC/dof_ledger.py, and you SHOULD report what should be logged.
key_patterns: Follow v1_lab/qm_detect.py exactly: pure-stdlib; module docstring stating scope + which rules are LOCKED vs which are tunable PARAMETERS/VARIANTS; parameters exposed via argparse with sensible defaults and a comment that they are 'tunable, not baked in'; a load_ohlc()-style tolerant CSV reader (header 'datetime,open,high,low,close,volume'; datetime formats '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' and '%Y.%m.%d %H:%M'); Wilder ATR via atr_wilder(); confirmed swings via detect_swings() with a strict L/R pivot; causal forward sweep with 'most recent confirmed swing' pointers (a swing at index t is only confirmed at t+pivot); a selfcheck() with synthetic bars proving BOTH the positive case and the negative case (e.g. body-close vs wick) AND that a gate is the discriminator (toggle it off and the event reappears); print_summary() with detection counts; write_*_csv() deterministic output. Reuse detect_swings/atr_wilder/load_ohlc from qm_detect.py rather than reimplementing. The pipeline trade-CSV format is DIFFERENT (metrics.load_trades expects header 'time,profit', rows 'YYYY.MM.DD HH:MM,<net_profit>') - the variant runner must emit that exact format.

v1_lab/walkforward.py, v1_lab/regime.py, v1_lab/cost_stress.py, v1_lab/benchmark.py (validation infra - reuse, do not duplicate)

directory_structure: Repo root /projects/sandbox/ckrepo has many .mq5 EAs and .ps1 MT5-runner scripts (legacy, not touched). v1_lab/ = the Python validation lab and where all new blocks go (detectors, rule engine, variant runner, real OHLC CSVs, validation infra). SPEC/ = locked design docs + hash-chained ledger + knowledge gate. .agents/tasks/ = this plan.
locked_rules: IMPLEMENT EXACTLY (creator-confirmed / provable): MSS = body-CLOSE (not wick) beyond most-recent confirmed swing + displacement = body/ATR14. TF backbone H4->H1->M15->M5. XAUUSD only. Engine timezone = America/New_York (DST-aware) for the 8:30 and 9:30 legs; DISPLAY to user in IST. US DST = 2nd Sunday March to 1st Sunday November (EDT UTC-4) else EST UTC-5. Neither the 8:30 nor the 9:30 leg may be hard-coded as 'the manipulation' vs 'the expansion' - both are examined.
open_rules_are_variants: Do NOT lock or guess a winner for any of these; expose each as a parameter or variant switch with a sensible default: SMT pair (XAU-XAG vs XAU-DXY vs off; + rolling-correlation guard to skip false SMT); POI type (QM left-shoulder vs +OB vs +FVG confluence); SL (Head/SMT-high+buffer vs tighter POI; buffer = ATR-multiple param); TP (full opposite-EXTERNAL vs fixed-RR vs partial/BE/trail; min projected-RR gate param); IDM clear (mandatory=A+ vs optional=experimental); swing pivot L/R count (param, default 2); ERL source TF (param); max-trades/day & re-entry (risk params); session scope (NY-only vs also London/Asia).
data_dependency: SMT variant needs XAGUSD and DXY OHLC series aligned to XAUUSD timestamps. These are NOT in the repo yet. The SMT block/variant must be built to accept an optional second-series CSV and, when absent, cleanly report the data dependency and disable the SMT variant (variant = OFF) rather than fabricating data. User can export XAGUSD/DXY from MT5 in the same 'datetime,open,high,low,close,volume' format as the existing files.
